To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of spectral properties, vegetation indexes and crop row detection is helpful for the prediction of weeds, and that the semi-supervised classifier is able to perform well in the classification problem assessed using only a small amount of information provided by the farmer.

(i) the use of a semi-supervised system allows to obtain good weed maps using very few labelled images (ii) the combination of spectral properties of pixels with vegetation indexes and the crop row detection method helps to improve the weed mapping results and (iii) the proposed method could be extended to other crops.
a semi-supervised system based on the combination of vegetation indexes and crop row detection is an efficient method to map weeds.

the problem of weed detection in sunflower crops.
the problem of constructing a mapping model via machine-learning techniques for weed detection in sunflower crops.
a new method for weed mapping using a combination of spectral information and vegetation indexes, crop rows and machine learning techniques, which are assessed in sunflower crops.

the proposed system is a promising tool for weed mapping.
a semi-supervised system using a combination of spectral properties, vegetation indexes and crop row detection can perform well for weed mapping in precision agriculture.

a semi-supervised system can be used for weed mapping in precision agriculture, which could be applied to other crops.
the use of a semi-supervised classifier, combined with vegetation indexes and a method to detect crop rows, provides a good performance for the weed mapping problem, using imagery provided with UAVs.

the use of a semi-supervised system, which combines spectral information with other information such as vegetation indexes and crop row detection, is a promising alternative for weed mapping in precision agriculture.
